questions.q: What is P(A or B) for any two events? [1.4]
questions.explain:
Paragraph 1.4: The overlap would otherwise be counted twice.
B is wrong: That holds only for disjoint events.
C is wrong: That is P(A and B) for independent events.
D is wrong: That is the complement of A.

questions.q: With two fair dice, what is the probability of a total of seven? [1.5]
questions.explain:
Paragraph 1.5: Six of the thirty-six equally likely outcomes total seven.
A is wrong: There are six ways, not three.
C is wrong: Only six outcomes total seven.
D is wrong: That is one specific ordered outcome.

questions.q: How many five-card hands can be dealt from a 52-card deck? [1.8]
questions.explain:
Paragraph 1.8: Order does not matter in a hand.
A is wrong: That counts ordered draws with replacement.
B is wrong: That counts ordered hands.
C is wrong: That is 52 × 5.

questions.q: In a room of twenty-three people, about what is the chance that at least two share a birthday? [1.9]
options: Just over one half, about 50.7 per cent
questions.explain:
Paragraph 1.9: The chance all differ is about 0.493.
B is wrong: That is roughly 23/365.
C is wrong: Pairs grow much faster than people.
D is wrong: Certainty needs 366 people.

questions.q: A product has one hundred components, each with a 1 per cent chance of a defect. About what is the chance of at least one defect? [1.11]
questions.explain:
Paragraph 1.11: 1 − 0.99¹⁰⁰ ≈ 0.634.
A is wrong: Small risks add up.
C is wrong: It is not certain.
D is wrong: That is the chance of no defect.

quizzes.title: Conditional Probability, Independence, and Bayes' Theorem

questions.q: About what is the probability of drawing two aces without replacement? [2.2]
questions.explain:
Paragraph 2.2: After the first ace, three aces remain among fifty-one cards.
A is wrong: That assumes replacement.
B is wrong: Probabilities of a sequence multiply.
D is wrong: That is one ace.

questions.q: Two machines make 60 and 40 per cent of parts with defect rates 1 and 3 per cent. What is the overall defect rate? [2.4]
questions.explain:
Paragraph 2.4: 0.6 × 1% + 0.4 × 3% = 0.6% + 1.2% = 1.8%.
A is wrong: That is the unweighted average.
B is wrong: That adds the rates.
C is wrong: That is only the second machine's contribution.

questions.q: Ten independent components, each 99 per cent reliable, are in series. About how reliable is the system? [2.7]
questions.explain:
Paragraph 2.7: 0.99¹⁰ ≈ 0.904; every component must work.
B is wrong: Series reliability is the product.
C is wrong: That would be a redundant system.
D is wrong: The product is far larger.

questions.q: A disease affects 1 per cent; a test detects 99 per cent of cases and gives 2 per cent false positives. What is P(disease | positive)? [2.10]
questions.explain:
Paragraph 2.10: Of 297 positives per 10,000, 99 are true.
A is wrong: That ignores the base rate.
B is wrong: That is the false-positive rate.
C is wrong: False positives outnumber true ones two to one.

questions.q: In the Monty Hall problem, what is the probability of winning if you switch? [2.13]
questions.explain:
Paragraph 2.13: Your first choice was right only one third of the time.
A is wrong: The host's knowledge makes the doors unequal.
C is wrong: That is the chance if you stay.
D is wrong: Switching can still lose.

questions.q: What is the expected value of a fair die? [3.2]
questions.explain:
Paragraph 3.2: (1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6)/6 = 3.5; it need not be a possible value.
B is wrong: The average of 1 to 6 is 3.5.
C is wrong: That is the maximum.
D is wrong: That is the sum, not divided by six.

questions.q: Which formula gives the variance of X? [3.4]
questions.explain:
Paragraph 3.4: For a fair die it is 35/12, about 2.92.
A is wrong: The square of the mean alone is not the variance.
B is wrong: The order is reversed.
D is wrong: The square of the mean is subtracted.

questions.q: Parts have a 2 per cent defect rate; an inspector samples twenty. About what is the chance of no defectives? [3.7]
questions.explain:
Paragraph 3.7: 0.98²⁰ ≈ 0.668; the expected number is 0.4.
A is wrong: That is one part.
B is wrong: 0.4 is the expected number of defectives.
D is wrong: That is the defect rate.

questions.q: If each attempt succeeds with probability 1/10, how many attempts are needed on average? [3.8]
questions.explain:
Paragraph 3.8: The geometric distribution has mean 1/p.
A is wrong: 1/p = 10.
B is wrong: That is 1/p².
D is wrong: Most attempts fail.

questions.q: A server averages three requests per second. About what is the probability of none in a given second? [3.11]
questions.explain:
Paragraph 3.11: The Poisson probability of zero is e^(−λ).
A is wrong: That is the probability of exactly three.
B is wrong: No requests is possible.
C is wrong: That is 1/3, not e⁻³.

quizzes.title: Continuous Distributions and the Central Limit Theorem

questions.q: If requests arrive at three per second, what is the mean time between them? [4.4]
questions.explain:
Paragraph 4.4: Exponential waiting times have mean 1/λ.
A is wrong: That inverts the rate.
C is wrong: The rate is three per second.
D is wrong: That is a probability, not a mean.

questions.q: What does it mean that the exponential distribution is memoryless? [4.5]
options: The chance of surviving another t hours does not depend on how long the item has lasted
questions.explain:
Paragraph 4.5: It suits components in useful life, not parts that wear out.
A is wrong: They vary randomly.
B is wrong: That is wear-out, not memorylessness.
C is wrong: Its mean is 1/λ.

questions.q: About what fraction of a normal distribution lies within two standard deviations of the mean? [4.7]
questions.explain:
Paragraph 4.7: The 68–95–99.7 rule.
A is wrong: That is within one.
B is wrong: That is within three.
C is wrong: Half lies on each side of the mean.

questions.q: What is the standard error of the mean of n independent measurements with standard deviation σ? [4.10]
questions.explain:
Paragraph 4.10: Variances add, so the variance of the mean is σ²/n.
B is wrong: Precision improves only with the square root.
C is wrong: Averaging reduces spread.
D is wrong: That is the spread of the sum.

questions.q: What does the central limit theorem state? [4.12]
options: The distribution of a sample mean of many independent variables with finite variance approaches a normal distribution
Sample means always equal the true mean
questions.explain:
Paragraph 4.12: This holds whatever the shape of each variable's distribution.
A is wrong: Only sums and averages approach normality.
C is wrong: That is approached by the law of large numbers.
D is wrong: That is not the theorem.

questions.q: Why does the sample variance divide by n − 1? [5.2]
options: Because one measurement is always discarded
To make the variance larger than any data value
To estimate the population variance without bias, since deviations are measured from the sample mean
questions.explain:
Paragraph 5.2: The sample mean estimates the population mean.
A is wrong: No data are discarded.
B is wrong: That is not the purpose.
D is wrong: n is known.

questions.q: A coin lands heads k times in n tosses. What is the maximum likelihood estimate of p? [5.4]
questions.explain:
Paragraph 5.4: Maximising p^k (1 − p)^(n − k) gives p̂ = k/n.
A is wrong: The estimate depends on the data.
C is wrong: That inverts the ratio.
D is wrong: That is the odds.

questions.q: With known σ, what is a 95 per cent confidence interval for the mean of normal data? [5.5]
questions.explain:
Paragraph 5.5: 1.96 standard errors either side of the sample mean.
A is wrong: The standard error σ/√n is needed.
B is wrong: The multiplier and the square root are missing.
C is wrong: That is a different rule.

questions.q: A poll of one thousand finds 50 per cent support. About what is the 95 per cent margin of error? [5.8]
questions.explain:
Paragraph 5.8: Standard error √(0.25/1000) ≈ 1.6 points; doubled gives about 3.
A is wrong: That is one standard error.
B is wrong: Far too wide for n = 1000.
D is wrong: Far too narrow.

questions.q: What can be said directly of a Bayesian 95 per cent credible interval? [5.11]
options: It is identical to a confidence interval in meaning
It contains 95 per cent of the data
Given the data and the prior, there is a 95 per cent probability the parameter lies in it
questions.explain:
Paragraph 5.11: A confidence interval does not allow that statement for a single interval.
A is wrong: Their interpretations differ.
B is wrong: It concerns the parameter.
D is wrong: It depends on the prior.

quizzes.title: Hypothesis Testing, Regression, and Engineering Statistics

questions.q: What is a p-value? [6.2]
options: The probability, assuming the null hypothesis, of a statistic at least as extreme as observed
The probability that the null hypothesis is true
The probability the result is important
questions.explain:
Paragraph 6.2: A small p-value counts as evidence against the null.
B is wrong: That is a common misreading.
C is wrong: Significance is not importance.
D is wrong: That is chosen in advance.

questions.q: A coin tossed 400 times gives 225 heads. What is the standardised value under fairness? [6.3]
questions.explain:
Paragraph 6.3: Mean 200 and standard deviation 10, so (225 − 200)/10 = 2.5.
B is wrong: One must divide by the standard deviation.
C is wrong: The standard deviation is 10, not 100.
D is wrong: The standard deviation is √(400 × 0.25) = 10.

questions.q: What is a type I error? [6.4]
options: Failing to reject a false null
Rejecting a true null hypothesis: a false alarm
questions.explain:
Paragraph 6.4: Its probability is the significance level.
A is wrong: That is type II.
C is wrong: That is power.
D is wrong: That affects power, not the definition.

questions.q: If twenty independent tests are run at the 5 per cent level with no real effects, about what is the chance of at least one false alarm? [6.7]
questions.explain:
Paragraph 6.7: 1 − 0.95²⁰ ≈ 0.64.
A is wrong: That is per test.
B is wrong: It is not certain.
C is wrong: Probabilities do not simply multiply by twenty here.

questions.q: What is the slope of the least-squares regression line? [6.9]
options: The covariance of x and y divided by the variance of x
The variance of y divided by the variance of x
The mean of y divided by the mean of x
questions.explain:
Paragraph 6.9: The line passes through the point of means.
A is wrong: Correlation is unitless.
C is wrong: The covariance is needed.
D is wrong: That ignores co-variation.
